keyFindings.description: The text the fix makes false is not on this branch's diff: skills/envoy/SKILL.md:136-140 still says a publish to a topic the publisher subscribes to is 'delivered to nobody' (core NATS does not skip the sender, so an ad-hoc topic now echoes to the publisher), and tool-contract.ts:180 still advertises envoy_publish as 'to any topic' though api.go:598 now answers 400 outside notifications. Not this issue's: dispatch://INFRA-113's approved spec (v12) names that text as its own deliverable ('the Envoy skill and the description of the envoy_publish tool say so'; #2101 'also changes the text that the fix made false'), and INFRA-117's spec delivers three code changes and says to adopt #2102's commit as it stands. Carrying the text here would also collide with INFRA-113's identical edits when dispatch://INFRA-120 merges this branch into main, where those files are untouched by this diff and main's copies win. Reported to the architect so the gap keeps its owner.

keyFindings.description: Census re-run at the head found two hits the table does not list: packages/envoy/scripts/e2e-local.sh:315,329 (publishes notifications.role.<role> only, unaffected; CI job envoy-e2e-local is green at 7424e75a, which is live proof) and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-11-enable-tsnet-listener.md:167,189,199 (a historical plan whose manual probes name test.security/test.health, which would now answer 400 instead of reaching NATS). Neither changes the census's finding: no production caller on this branch publishes outside notifications. The census also carries no explicit rollout line; the rollout is an immediate refusal, and the vulnerability it closes is named in dispatch://INFRA-113's approved spec (a token holder could publish to $KV.envoy_roles.<key> and rewrite which session holds a role).

The prefix check admits a topic whose tokens are literal NATS wildcards (notifications.> or notifications.*); under the widened grant both answer 200. The tester measured the effect: delivered only to a subscriber whose own pattern matches the literal token, never fanned out to subscribers of concrete topics, so it is amplification at most and not escalation (the same caller may publish each topic one by one). Hardening, and it belongs to the main-line fix if it is taken at all.

Both thermonuclear passes propose the same two simplifications: usesCoreTransport's first two clauses are now decided by the third (every role lane is a notifications. topic the stream never captures, pinned by TestStreamConfigExcludesRoleLanes), and streamCaptures hand-rolls a second, weaker subject matcher beside stream.go's subjectsOverlap, needing TestEveryStreamSubjectIsALiteralPrefixAndWildcard to hold its shape assumption up. Neither changes behaviour. The implementer's ce-simplify-code pass reached both and skipped both on the stated criterion of this issue, equivalence with the main-line fix; the hunks are byte-identical to #2101's, so applying them only here would diverge the branch it exists to mirror. They belong to dispatch://INFRA-113, mirrored back.
